topic: AutoMat human-SME judge calibration is strong but revision- and domain-scoped

paper.title: Can Coding Agents Reproduce Findings in Computational Materials Science?
facts: AutoMat calibrates its automated evaluator against blinded judgments from qualified subject-matter experts on a stratified subset of n=40 runs covering different agent systems and claim types.

SMEs are given the same task materials, execution traces and produced artifacts used for evaluation, but do not see the agent final answer, agent self-evaluation, or LLM judge assessment, explicitly to reduce anchoring.
The automated evaluator obtains quadratic-weighted kappa 0.69 and within-1-difference accuracy 0.80 against these SME judgments.

The paper explicitly cautions that automated judgment is a scalable approximation to expert assessment rather than a replacement, and names cross-domain/claim-type expansion and larger human evaluation as future work.
paper.scope: Computational materials science AutoMat claims and the sampled calibration runs; no universal evaluator-authority claim.

public_code.release_relation: The only observed public commit touching harness/evaluators/llm_repro_evaluator.py is the public initial-release commit, which postdates arXiv v1 by about six weeks.

facts: Current public evaluator has an explicit anchored 1-5 rubric and five fixed dimensions.
Current public evaluator may receive the agent analysis_result self-assessment and is instructed to compare its judgment with that self-assessment when available.

public_code.attribution_boundary: The observed public code is a post-paper initial release. Without a calibration manifest binding the n=40 SME judgments to exact evaluator model revision, prompt/rubric bytes and code revision, do not infer that the public c16a... evaluator bytes are exactly those whose kappa/within-1 metrics were measured.

derived_scope_limited_findings.claim: Human calibration materially strengthens AutoMat evaluator evidence: blinded SMEs on n=40 produce reported quadratic-weighted kappa 0.69 and within-1 accuracy 0.80. That supports benchmark-scale approximate judgment in the tested AutoMat scope, not final scientific authority or cross-domain substitutability.

A calibrated judge is revision-specific evidence. The public evaluator implementation was released after the paper submission, and the public surface observed here does not bind the reported SME calibration sample/results to exact evaluator code, model revision, prompt/rubric digest and input-snapshot protocol. Any drift in those components should invalidate automatic inheritance of the old calibration certificate until revalidated.

Calibration input protocol itself is part of judge identity. AutoMat's SMEs were blinded to agent final answer/self-evaluation/judge output, whereas the current automated evaluator can explicitly receive and compare against agent self-assessment. This does not make the calibration invalid, but it means human-vs-LLM agreement cannot be interpreted as a matched-input interchangeability experiment.

protocol_implication.name: CALIBRATED_JUDGE_SCOPE_AND_REVISION_GATE
protocol_implication.rule: A judge-calibration certificate binds evaluator code/model/prompt/rubric/input-exposure policy, calibration dataset/run snapshot, human blinding protocol, scientific domain/claim-type coverage and calibration metrics. Reuse as 'calibrated' requires an exact matching evaluator fingerprint and in-scope target; otherwise label the current judge uncalibrated/changed-revision and require fresh calibration before giving the old certificate authority. Human-calibrated automated scores remain downstream evidence, not final scientific truth.

causal_boundary: No new agent-performance effect is claimed and no defect in the reported kappa calculation is alleged.
